newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - June 3.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:
DENVER - Timothy McVeigh was convicted of the worst act of domestic terrorism in American history, the bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City.
WASHINGTON - For federal workers, the guilty verdicts returned against Timothy McVeigh don't end the pain of losing loved ones or co-workers in the deadly blast.
WASHINGTON - The bombing of the Oklahoma City federal building was such a unique and awful event that at first Americans could not believe it was home-grown.
WASHINGTON - Several cable and broadcast television networks are preparing to modify a controversial new ratings system to include on-screen symbols for sexual material, violence or foul language.
PARIS - Lionel Jospin was named prime minister of France today by President Jacques Chirac, the man who most wanted to keep Jospin out of office and who threatens to thwart his agenda at every turn.
SHAWNIGAN, QUEBEC - Canadians voted in a national election that was expected to give a new but possibly weak mandate to Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberal Party.
